subject: Dedicated fleet: traffic shape, token-length sampler and burst windows
messages:
From: Erin Park <erin@asteriahealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@asteriahealth.com
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated fleet: initial traffic snapshot request

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the predictable latency profile. Procurement asked for a short traffic snapshot so we can evaluate committed capacity sizing. Can you send a concise questionnaire that captures: typical concurrency, burst windows, prompt length / completion length distribution, and any sampling you recommend for live telemetry? We can attach a CSV sample from our logs if that helps.

High level constraints: P99 latency target 250ms for chat flows, and we want to cap dedicated spend to a predictable monthly commit.

Thanks,
Erin Park
Head of Platform, Asteria Health
Erin.Park@asteriahealth.com

---
Attachment: none
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Erin Park <erin@asteriahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet: initial traffic snapshot request

Erin — thanks, happy to help. Attached is a short sampler we use for pre-sales sizing (CSV template) plus a two-page checklist that maps answers to an initial GPU-pool recommendation. To speed this up, could you fill the CSV with a week sample (UTC timestamps preferred) and answer the 6 quick bullets below? If you prefer, we can run a 30-min telemetry call to pull a sample directly from your logs.

Quick bullets (please paste short answers):
- Primary workload(s) (chat / async generation / embeddings / reranking):
- Typical concurrency (avg concurrent sessions) and observed daily peak concurrency:
- Burst characteristics (hours of day, fraction of daily traffic in bursts, burst duration typical):
- Prompt length distribution (median, 75th, 95th in tokens) and completion/response lengths:
- Average tokens per API call and percent of calls that use streaming:
- SLA tolerances (P50/P95/P99 targets) and acceptable fallbacks (e.g., switch to a cheaper smaller model):

What I attached:
- asteria_token_sample.csv (CSV template with columns: timestamp, endpoint, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, session_id, model)
- dedicated_sizer_checklist.pdf (one-page mapping matrix: token-mix -> GPU SKU suggestion -> batching guidance)

Next steps after you return the CSV: we’ll run a quick sizing sim and propose a reserved pool + canary routing policy.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated fleet: initial traffic snapshot request

FW: Erin at Asteria needs the sampler filled and procurement has budget questions. Quick notes for you both:
- Target P99 250ms — that's tight for chat with long completions; plan to propose an MPS-l1-ish SKU + headroom for bursts.
- If their median prompt is small (<64 tokens) and completions average <128, we can lean on a smaller quantized model and pack more sessions per GPU.
- Ben: please prep a short cost/backstop note that outlines canary fallback to hosted API and monthly commit tiers (3/6/12mo).
- Monica: can you own running the sizing sim once we get their CSV? I’ll take the token distribution and batching knobs.

Thanks — we should keep this tight; procurement wants an internal doc by Friday.

-Aditya

Internal-only forward, no attachments
From: Erin Park <erin@asteriahealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@asteriahealth.com
Date: Thu, 13 Mar 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet: initial traffic snapshot request

Aditya — attached is a 7-day export from our staging traffic (anonymized session ids). Notes inline below and summarized at the end.

Inline answers:
- Primary workload(s): chat + short batch generation for summaries (approx 80/20 split).
- Typical concurrency: avg 120 concurrent sessions; observed daily peak 1,150 during US east morning (07:00-09:00 ET).
- Burst characteristics: 07:00-09:30 local (roughly 14% of daily traffic in that 2.5h window); occasional midday bump at 12:30-13:00 (5% of daily). Burst durations range 15m-90m.
- Prompt length distribution: median prompt 42 tokens; 75th=96; 95th=420 tokens. Completion/response lengths: median 110 tokens; 75th=220; 95th=900 tokens.
- Avg tokens per API call: 152 tokens. ~18% of calls use streaming (longer responses).
- SLA tolerances: tight for P99 (250ms) on interactive chat; P95 can be 140ms; acceptable fallback is to degrade to a smaller model (latency-optimized) for non-PCI sensitive sessions.

Attachments included: asteria_token_sample.csv, asteria_sla_requirements.pdf

Summary: attached CSV has the 7-day UTC export. Let us know if you want a full production pull — we can schedule access with engineering.

Thanks,
Erin

Attachment: asteria_token_sample.csv (7-day export, anonymized)
Attachment: asteria_sla_requirements.pdf
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Erin Park <erin@asteriahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, procurement@asteriahealth.com
Date: Thu, 13 Mar 2025 16:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet: initial traffic snapshot request

Erin — perfect, thanks for the fast turnaround and the CSV. I pulled an initial token-mix summary and ran a short sim; preliminary findings below (we’ll follow up with the full run and cost options):

Preliminary sizing summary (quick take):
- Recommended starting pool: 6 x gX-96 (high-memory latency-optimized) with quantized LLM variant for chat; this trades marginally higher monthly commit for headroom to meet P99 250ms in your east morning burst.
- Expected effective concurrency per GPU (median prompt mix): ~140 sessions/GPU with aggressive batching; during peak burst we estimate queueing and 15–25% routing to canary fallback (hosted low-latency model) if strict P99 must be enforced.
- Token economics: with your observed 152 tokens/api-call avg, token-cost per 1M calls maps to X spend (will include exact numbers in the detailed proposal).

Next steps:
1) Monica to run the full sizing sim and attach a config (ETA: EOD tomorrow).
2) Ben to prepare three commit tiers (3/6/12mo) with fallback pricing and an SLA appendix.
3) We’ll schedule a 30-min call with your eng team if you can provide temporary log access; otherwise, we’ll rely on the 7-day CSV.

Can we plan a check-in on Friday 09:00 PT? I’ll send a calendar invite after you confirm.

Thanks again — will follow up with the detailed workbook.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
